comment: Tests allowed to fail once and pass on retry without failing the job. Everything else that flakes fails CI. This list is debt: each entry is a test that is lying about the product, and it should shrink, never grow. Adding an entry is a deliberate decision that needs a reason and a date, not a way to get a red build green.
allow: virtualization.spec.ts › 08 — cascading older pages never snap the viewport toward newest
blocks.spec.ts › all 11 native primitives and the 10 bundled composites render through MessageRow
persistent-agent-audience.spec.ts › timeline agent send remains one-shot and returns to the placeholder

notes.virtualization.spec.ts › 08 — cascading: Added 2026-08-27. This is NOT a slow assertion: the run reports maxDrift 118 against a 5px bar, so the viewport really does snap toward newest under CI CPU contention. It reproduced on two consecutive runs of an unrelated PR (168 passed, this one flaked), and it currently blocks every PR against develop, including a production fix for agents leaking across communities. Listed to unblock that, not because it is understood. The drift is a real product symptom and this entry should be removed with a fix, not renewed.
notes.blocks.spec.ts › all 11 native primitive: Added 2026-08-27. The Gate B screenshot walk (blocks.spec.ts:90) intermittently misses one state (observed: proposal-failed.png) and then passes on retry. Reproduced the same way on two unrelated PRs the same afternoon (#476 buzz-acp-only, #477 desktop-only), so it is CI CPU contention, not either diff. Not understood; listed to unblock develop. Should be removed with a fix (state wait before the Gate B screenshot assert), not renewed.
notes.persistent-agent-audience.spec.ts › time: Added 2026-09-01. Typing immediately after selecting a mention intermittently loses the chip's trailing space: expected "@Morgarita hello", got "@Morgaritahello". Three test-side fixes were tried and two were wrong. toHaveText("@Morgarita ") normalises whitespace, so it also matches "@Morgarita" and guarded nothing. A textContent poll then proved the space had landed but said nothing about the caret. The current guard polls both text and atDocumentEnd, is proven load-bearing (forcing the caret condition false fails the test), and it PASSED on the run that then failed at the next line - so the space is present and the caret is at the document end when typing starts, and the space is lost afterwards. That rules out the insert itself: replacePlainTextRange commits "@Morgarita " and the caret in one transaction. The remaining suspect is usePersistentAgentMentionHydration, which calls replacePlainTextRange as well and can rewrite the composer while the user types. If that is right this is a product bug - hydration clobbering in-flight input - and the spec is reporting it correctly. Listed to stop it blocking releases a fourth time, not because it is understood. Remove with a fix to the hydration race, not by renewing this entry.
